job.title: Head of Marketing - Live Entertainment & Major Events!
job.description:
An exciting opportunity to lead the marketing strategy behind live entertainment, arts and cultural experiences is available!

If you love figuring out what makes the customer tick, knowing why people buy a ticket and turn up, and you’re just as excited about helping a team get better at that work, then this could be a great next step for you.

The opportunity:

We’re partnering with an entertainment marketing consultancy that works as an extension of its clients’ teams across live performance, culture and major events. As Head of Marketing, you’ll join the senior leadership team and be the person key clients turn to for strategic advice.

Most of your time will be spent on client strategy and relationships. You’ll also lead and mentor account directors and senior account managers, improve how the team works and support the wider consultancy in winning new business.

What you’ll do:

  • Own the marketing strategy for key accounts, using audience insight to set clear objectives and guide creative, media and content through to delivery.
  • Build trusted relationships with senior clients and work with digital and audience specialists to turn campaign results into clear recommendations.
  • Coach account directors and managers to sharpen their strategy, write stronger briefs and develop their leadership skills.
  • Improve how work moves across teams, from briefing and onboarding to clearer ownership on shared accounts.
  • Lead campaign budgets, forecasting and account performance, and contribute to pitches, proposals and growth opportunities with existing clients.

What you’ll bring:

  • At least eight years’ experience in senior marketing roles. Live entertainment or theatre is ideal, and we’d also love to hear from you if you’ve grown audiences for film, music, sport, festivals, attractions or tourism.
  • A track record of setting audience-led strategy and building trusted relationships with senior clients or stakeholders.
  • Experience leading and developing teams, with examples of how you’ve improved the way they work.
  • A strong grasp of digital, social and paid media, plus the commercial judgement to manage budgets and measure results.
  • Agency or consultancy experience is highly regarded, if you've been a marketing selling experiences, I'd love to talk to you.

The role includes occasional East Coast travel and some evenings at shows, openings and industry events. You’ll also have access to regular show and event tickets, mentoring and professional development.

You’ll join a team that enjoys working together, backs each other and makes time to celebrate the wins. There’s a genuine focus on wellbeing, with recent activities including sound baths and blender bike sessions. The team also gets together for offsite strategy lunches, giving everyone a chance to step away from the day-to-day and make space for bigger-picture strategic thinking.

Apply If this sounds like your next chapter, we’d love to hear from you.

job.title: Studio Growth Coordinator - Architecture & Design Industry
job.description:
Love taking a brief, pulling together input from busy project teams and turning it into a bid that’s clear, persuasive and beautifully presented? This role gives you the chance to do that while getting involved in the marketing and business development work that helps a design practice keep on growing!

The Practice:

New Chapter Talent is partnering with an established multidisciplinary architecture and design practice. Its teams work across a range of sectors, including education, health, residential, sport and recreation, and public spaces, based in Melbourne CBD.

The Opportunity:

You’ll work closely with studio leaders, project teams and the national marketing and business development team. Bids and submissions are central to the role, with scope to tell the stories behind the practice’s projects and help the team pursue new work.

  • Coordinate bids, tenders, proposals and capability statements, keeping contributors and deadlines on track.
  • Write and edit submission content that makes the practice’s experience and design approach clear to prospective clients.
  • Use Adobe InDesign to produce polished, on-brand submissions, presentations and marketing materials.
  • Support awards entries, digital content, studio communications and thought leadership.
  • Keep CRM records up to date and help studio leaders identify and pursue new business opportunities.

About you:

You’ve prepared bids, tenders or proposals in architecture, design or a related professional services environment. You’re a confident writer with an eye for layout, and you know how to get the information you need from busy people to meet a deadline, you'll be passionate about bringing you work to life through social media, and using storytelling via LinkedIn and other platforms to showcase the brand.

  • Hands-on experience with Adobe InDesign and Microsoft Office.
  • Strong writing, editing and proofreading skills.
  • The ability to juggle multiple deadlines and work collaboratively with senior leaders and project teams.
  • Experience with a CRM is well regarded.

What’s on offer

  • A permanent role with a 37.5-hour full-time week or part-time hours across a minimum of four days.
  • Exposure to a variety of projects and sectors, with the opportunity to contribute to both submissions and broader studio growth.
  • Structured mentoring, professional development and study leave for approved learning.

To submit an application for this role, please submit your CV via APPLY NOW.
